| `messaging`        | 5         |
| `metrics-claimed`  | 5         |
| `logos`            | 5         |
| `pricing`          | 1         |

Rows within each section are ordered by `discovered_at` DESC (newest

Sections included: `blog-posts`, `press-posts`, `case-studies`,
`job-listings`, `ads`, `pricing`, `messaging`, `metrics-claimed`, `logos`,

403 if deactivated, 404 if cross-tenant or unknown.

data.current_description:
Returns activity across the workspace's active competitors.

Window behaviour depends on `from` / `to`:
  * Omit BOTH `from` and `to` → the complete all-time roster, including items
    that already existed when tracking began (the initial backfill). For
    versioned sections (job-listings, ads, logos, messaging, pricing) this is
    the current live snapshot, not removed history; on this path
    `change_type=added` therefore covers essentially the whole roster and
    `total` is the all-time count.
  * Supply `from` (and/or `to`) → adds / updates / removals in that window only
    (defaults: `from` = 30d ago, `to` = now), excluding backfill.

`sitemap-urls` is the one exception to the backfill rule above: it excludes
`initial_run` items on BOTH paths, so the all-time count for that section
matches what the window path reports rather than including the URLs that were
already present when tracking began.

`sitemap-urls` is also the highest-volume section by a wide margin - a single
crawl can append several hundred URLs for one competitor, and because they are
the most recent rows they land at the front of an unfiltered feed. If you are
after other kinds of change, narrow with `?section=` rather than paging past
them.

To keep list rows lean, the bulky fields `description`, `key_points`,
`pricing_data`, and `excerpt` are OMITTED from each item's `data` here. Fetch
the full payload for a row via `GET /activity/{row_uuid}` or, in batch, via
`GET /activity/items`.

Any `competitor_id` referencing a deactivated competitor yields a 403.
data.summary_suggestion: List competitor activity changes with optional time window
data.description_suggestion: Returns activity (additions, updates, removals) across the workspace's active competitors. Behavior depends on time window parameters: omit both `from` and `to` to retrieve the complete all-time roster including initial backfill; supply `from` and/or `to` (defaults: 30 days ago to now) to retrieve only changes within that window, excluding backfill. For versioned sections (job-listings, ads, logos, messaging, pricing), all-time queries return current live snapshots. Note: `sitemap-urls` excludes initial_run items on both paths and is high-volume (hundreds of URLs per crawl); use `?section=` to filter if needed. Response items omit bulky fields (`description`, `key_points`, `pricing_data`, `excerpt`) - use `GET /activity/{row_uuid}` or `GET /activity/items` to fetch full payloads. Returns 403 if any referenced competitor is deactivated.

This structure helps AI agents quickly understand when and how to use the operation.

data.current_description:
Batch sibling of `GET /activity/{row_uuid}` — resolves one-or-more row UUIDs
to their full (untrimmed) payloads in a single request. Use it to drill into
several rows spotted in the lean `GET /activity` list without N round-trips.

Partial success is normal: ids that don't resolve (unknown, in another
workspace, recorded during an inactive period, or malformed) are returned in
`not_found` rather than failing the call. The `data` array order is NOT
guaranteed — match results back to your request by `id`.
data.description_suggestion: Batch lookup of multiple activity rows by UUID to retrieve their full (untrimmed) payloads in a single request. Use to efficiently drill into several rows spotted in the lean `GET /activity` list without multiple round-trips. Supports partial success: IDs that don't resolve (unknown, cross-workspace, recorded during inactive period, or malformed) are returned in `not_found` rather than failing the entire call. Returns a `data` array with resolved rows and a `not_found` array with unresolved IDs; note that `data` array order is not guaranteed—match results back to your request by `id` field.
data.reasoning: Summary is clear and action-oriented. Description explains the operation well but lacks explicit detail about the response structure (data array + not_found array). Added clarity about return format to help AI agents understand what to expect and how to parse the response.

data.current_description:
Returns activity across the workspace's active competitors.

Window behaviour depends on `from` / `to`:
  * Omit BOTH `from` and `to` → the complete all-time roster, including items
    that already existed when tracking began (the initial backfill). For
    versioned sections (job-listings, ads, logos, messaging, pricing) this is
    the current live snapshot, not removed history; on this path
    `change_type=added` therefore covers essentially the whole roster and
    `total` is the all-time count.
  * Supply `from` (and/or `to`) → adds / updates / removals in that window only
    (defaults: `from` = 30d ago, `to` = now), excluding backfill.

`sitemap-urls` is the one exception to the backfill rule above: it excludes
`initial_run` items on BOTH paths, so the all-time count for that section
matches what the window path reports rather than including the URLs that were
already present when tracking began.

`sitemap-urls` is also the highest-volume section by a wide margin - a single
crawl can append several hundred URLs for one competitor, and because they are
the most recent rows they land at the front of an unfiltered feed. If you are
after other kinds of change, narrow with `?section=` rather than paging past
them.

To keep list rows lean, the bulky fields `description`, `key_points`,
`pricing_data`, and `excerpt` are OMITTED from each item's `data` here. Fetch
the full payload for a row via `GET /activity/{row_uuid}` or, in batch, via
`GET /activity/items`.

Any `competitor_id` referencing a deactivated competitor yields a 403.
data.summary_suggestion: Query cross-competitor activity changes or full roster
data.description_suggestion: Returns activity across the workspace's active competitors. Behavior depends on time window parameters: omit both `from` and `to` to retrieve the complete all-time roster (including initial backfill); supply `from` and/or `to` to retrieve only adds/updates/removals within that window (defaults: 30 days ago to now, excluding backfill). For versioned sections (job-listings, ads, logos, messaging, pricing), all-time queries return current live snapshots. Note: `sitemap-urls` excludes initial backfill on both paths and is high-volume (hundreds of URLs per crawl); use `?section=` to filter if needed. Response rows are trimmed (omitting `description`, `key_points`, `pricing_data`, `excerpt`); fetch full payloads via `GET /activity/{row_uuid}` or batch via `GET /activity/items`. Returns 403 if any competitor_id references a deactivated competitor.

data.current_description:
Batch sibling of `GET /activity/{row_uuid}` — resolves one-or-more row UUIDs
to their full (untrimmed) payloads in a single request. Use it to drill into
several rows spotted in the lean `GET /activity` list without N round-trips.

Partial success is normal: ids that don't resolve (unknown, in another
workspace, recorded during an inactive period, or malformed) are returned in
`not_found` rather than failing the call. The `data` array order is NOT
guaranteed — match results back to your request by `id`.
data.description_suggestion: Batch lookup of activity rows by UUID to retrieve full (untrimmed) payloads in a single request. Use to drill into multiple rows from the lean `GET /activity` list without N round-trips. Supports partial success: unresolvable IDs (unknown, cross-tenant, from inactive periods, or malformed) are returned in `not_found` rather than failing the call. The `data` array order is not guaranteed; match results back to your request by `id`. Returns full item payloads including previously-trimmed fields.
